concerns.text: Task T020a [US2] specifies an evaluation script that *may* use the wrong statistical test (Diebold‑Mariano). This directly weakens SC‑002, which the spec mandates must be measured with a **paired t‑test**. Planning to implement the wrong test violates the spec and must be removed or corrected before any deliverable.

SC‑004 (robustness of decision thresholds) lacks any concrete acceptance threshold in the spec, yet no task defines a pass/fail criterion (e.g., maximum allowable false‑positive variation). Dropping this acceptance criterion means the requirement cannot be verified.

The constitution (Principle II – Verified Accuracy) requires a task that invokes the Reference‑Validator Agent to verify all external citations. No such task exists in the current list, constituting a breach of the non‑negotiable constitution.

Principle I (Reproducibility) demands that all scripts pin random seeds. The random‑seed helper (T044) is still pending and no other task guarantees that every script imports and uses it. This omission weakens reproducibility guarantees.

Principle III (Data Hygiene) requires checksums for all raw and processed data files. Tasks T008a and T008b (checksum generation) are pending, and there is no downstream task that records these checksums in the project state file. Without them the data‑hygiene requirement is not satisfied.

Critical core artifacts needed for FR‑001 (data retrieval & preprocessing) and FR‑005 (independent validation) are still marked as pending (e.g., T005a‑T005c, T006d, T006a, T008a/b, T013, T023a). Their absence means the functional requirements cannot be fulfilled, effectively weakening the specification.
